t: A contractor inserts a clause in his agreement making the sub-contractor liable for any damage to materials at site. This is a method of:
e: Risk can be transferred by contract (hold-harmless or indemnity clauses) to another party without using insurance.

t: The Oriental Life Insurance Company (1818) is remembered for the fact that it:
o: Insured only Indian lives at standard rates
Charged Indian lives a higher (extra) premium than European lives
Was nationalised in 1956 to form LIC
e: Early British insurers treated Indian lives as sub-standard and loaded their premiums; Bombay Mutual (1870) first insured Indians at normal rates.

t: A factory risk of Rs 50 crore is co-insured, with Insurer P as leader for 60% and Insurer Q as follower for 40%. On a loss of Rs 10 crore, Q's share is:
e: In co-insurance each insurer is directly liable to the insured for its agreed percentage: 40% of Rs 10 crore = Rs 4 crore.

t: A policy condition requiring the insured to give written notice of loss within 7 days, failing which the insurer is not liable, is a:
e: Claim conditions such as timely notice are conditions precedent to the insurer's liability for that claim.

t: An insurer's retention is Rs 25 lakh and its surplus treaty provides 3 lines. The largest risk it can accept with the help of this treaty alone is:
e: Capacity = retention + (lines x retention) = Rs 25 lakh + 3 x Rs 25 lakh = Rs 1 crore.

t: A trader insures a consignment of smuggled goods against theft. The contract is:
o: Valid, since premium has been paid
Voidable at the option of the insurer
Void, because its object is unlawful
Valid if the goods are later legalised
e: An agreement with an unlawful object or consideration is void under the Indian Contract Act.

t: As per IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests norms, a general insurer must decide on a claim within how many days of receiving the final survey report?
e: The insurer must settle or reject the claim within 30 days of receipt of the final survey report and all documents.

t: A 17-year-old student signs a proposal form and pays premium for a policy in his own name. Under the Indian Contract Act, the agreement is:
o: Void, as a minor is not competent to contract
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 11 requires parties to have attained majority; an agreement with a minor is void ab initio.

t: Under the rule of 'contra proferentem', an ambiguity in a policy wording is interpreted:
o: Against the insurer who drafted it
Against the insured who accepted it
By reference to the Ombudsman alone
e: Because the policy is drafted by the insurer, any ambiguity is construed in favour of the insured.

t: A godown is insured for Rs 8 lakh under a fire policy without any average condition. A fire causes a loss assessed at Rs 10 lakh. The insurer pays:
e: The sum insured is the maximum liability of the insurer; the loss in excess of the sum insured is borne by the insured.

t: Large-scale unemployment caused by an economic recession is classified as a:
e: Fundamental risks arise from causes outside the control of any individual and affect large sections of society; particular risks affect individuals.

t: Under Section 12 of the Indian Contract Act, a person who is usually of unsound mind may make a valid contract:
o: At any time, with the consent of his doctor
During an interval when he is of sound mind
e: Capacity is judged at the time of contracting; a person usually of unsound mind can contract when he is of sound mind.

t: After an insurer settles a motor claim on a total loss basis, the damaged vehicle (wreck):
o: Remains with the insured free of charge
Must be handed over to the RTO
Becomes the property of the insurer as salvage
e: Having paid the full value, the insurer is entitled to the salvage, which is sold to reduce the net cost of the claim.

t: The gross (office) premium charged to a policyholder consists of:
o: Pure (risk) premium plus loadings for expenses, contingencies and profit
Claims paid in the previous year
e: The risk premium covers expected claims; loadings are added for management expenses, commission, contingencies and profit margin.

t: Private insurance companies were allowed to enter the Indian market after an interval of about four decades in the year:
e: Following the IRDA Act of 1999, the regulator issued the first registrations to private insurers in 2000.

t: Under Section 10 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which of the following is NOT an essential of a valid contract?
o: The agreement must be in writing
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A contract need not be written to be valid; the essentials are offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity, free consent and lawful object.

t: In insurance theory, the degree of risk is measured by:
o: The total number of policies issued
The size of the sum insured
The variation between actual losses and expected losses
e: Risk is the uncertainty of loss; the greater the possible deviation of actual from expected results, the higher the degree of risk.

t: A man insured under a personal accident policy falls from his horse, lies injured in a wet field, develops pneumonia and dies. His death is:
o: Not covered, since pneumonia is a disease
Covered only if he died within 24 hours
Not covered, since horse riding is hazardous
Covered, as the accident is the proximate cause of death
e: The chain of events was unbroken from the accidental fall to death, so the accident remains the proximate cause (Etherington case).

t: In a Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP), the investment risk in the fund is borne by:
e: In ULIPs the value of units fluctuates with market performance and the investment risk is borne by the policyholder.

t: Under the 'level premium' system in life insurance:
o: The premium remains constant throughout the term, with the early-year excess building reserves for later years
Premium increases every year with age
Premium is payable only in the first year
Premium is refunded if no claim arises
e: Since mortality rises with age, a level premium overcharges in early years and undercharges later; the excess forms the policy reserve.

t: The question 'Has any insurer ever declined, cancelled or refused to renew your insurance?' in a proposal form is mainly intended to assess:
e: Previous refusals, cancellations or special terms indicate how other insurers viewed the proposer's character and risk, i.e., moral hazard.

t: Arrange in correct chronological order: (i) Malhotra Committee report (ii) Entry of private insurers (iii) IRDA Act (iv) Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act
e: Malhotra report 1994, IRDA Act 1999, entry of private insurers 2000, Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015.

t: A fidelity guarantee policy taken by an employer covers:
o: Financial loss caused by dishonesty of employees
Injury to customers on the premises
Loss of profit after a fire
e: Fidelity guarantee insurance indemnifies the employer against loss of money or goods through fraud or dishonesty of employees.

t: A dry-cleaner takes a policy covering customers' garments held in his shop. He has insurable interest because:
o: As bailee, he is legally responsible for the goods in his custody
He owns the garments while they are with him
Customers have assigned their rights to him
Insurable interest is not necessary for goods of others
e: Bailees such as warehouse-keepers, repairers and carriers have insurable interest in goods entrusted to them.

t: In marine insurance, 'freight insurance' protects:
o: The cargo owner against damage to goods
The port against damage to its berths
The ship-owner against loss of freight earnings if cargo is not delivered
e: Marine insurance has three branches: hull, cargo and freight; freight insurance covers the carrier's earnings for carrying goods.

t: A bank has lent Rs 10 lakh to Ramesh. The bank's insurable interest in Ramesh's life is limited to:
o: The amount of the outstanding loan
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A creditor has insurable interest in the life of a debtor only to the extent of the debt.

t: Which statement about insurance is correct?
o: Insurance prevents the insured event from occurring
Insurance guarantees a profit to the insured on every loss
Insurance compensates the financial consequences of a loss but cannot prevent the loss event itself
e: Insurance does not remove or prevent risk; it provides financial compensation when an insured event occurs.

t: A broker licensed by IRDAI to arrange both direct insurance for clients and reinsurance for insurers is a:
e: IRDAI classifies brokers as direct, reinsurance and composite; composite brokers carry out both functions.

t: Before lodging his claim, Ravi signs a letter releasing the truck owner who damaged his car from all liability. The insurer may:
o: Do nothing, as the release does not affect the insurer
Pay the claim and still sue the truck owner
Recover the claim amount from the police
Reduce or refuse the claim, since its subrogation rights have been prejudiced
e: The insured must not do anything that prejudices the insurer's right of recovery against third parties.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, an award passed by the Ombudsman is:
o: Binding only if approved by IRDAI
e: The insurer must comply with the award within 30 days; the complainant remains free to pursue other remedies if dissatisfied.

t: Two fire policies of Rs 6 lakh each with Insurers A and B cover the same stock and each contains a 'rateable proportion' condition. On a loss of Rs 3 lakh, the insured claims from B alone. B is liable to pay:
e: The rateable proportion condition limits each insurer to its proportion of the loss, so B pays 6/12 of Rs 3 lakh = Rs 1.5 lakh.

t: An employer takes a 'keyman' life policy on the life of its chief technologist. The employer's insurable interest arises from:
o: The financial loss the employer would suffer on the employee's death
e: An employer has insurable interest in a key employee to the extent of the financial loss it would suffer on his death.

t: An additional benefit that pays an extra sum if death occurs due to accident, attached to a basic life policy for a small extra premium, is called a:
e: Riders are optional add-on benefits (accidental death, critical illness, waiver of premium) attached to a base life policy.

t: Which of the following is NOT normally a consideration in life insurance underwriting?
o: Cubic capacity of the proposer's car
e: Life underwriting considers age, health, occupation, habits, family history and financial standing; vehicle details relate to motor rating.

t: By paying premium, an insured essentially exchanges:
o: A small uncertain loss for a large certain cost
A large uncertain loss for a small certain cost
A certain loss for an uncertain gain
A speculative risk for a pure risk
e: Insurance substitutes certainty (the known premium) for uncertainty (the possible large loss), which is its core value to the insured.

t: In general insurance, the duty of disclosure of material facts operates:
o: Only at the inception of the first policy
Continuously every day during the policy period
Only when a claim is made
At inception and again at each renewal of the policy
e: Each renewal in general insurance is a fresh contract, so facts that have changed must be disclosed at that time.

t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

t: Which of the following is NOT a normal requirement for a risk to be insurable?
o: The loss must be measurable in money
The loss must be accidental and not intentional
There must be a large number of similar exposure units
The loss must be catastrophic, affecting a large number of insureds at the same time
e: Insurers need risks that are independent of each other; losses that strike many insureds simultaneously threaten the pool and are difficult to insure.

t: An insurer arranges for the damaged car of its policyholder to be put right at a garage and pays the garage bill directly. This method of indemnity is:
e: Indemnity may be provided by cash payment, repair, replacement or reinstatement; here the insurer provides indemnity by repair.

t: Which of the following was made possible by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015?
o: Foreign reinsurers could open branch offices in India
GIC was made the holding company of four subsidiaries
The Controller of Insurance was created
e: The 2015 amendment permitted foreign reinsurers and Lloyd's to set up branches in India, besides raising the foreign investment limit to 49%.

t: The duty of utmost good faith in an insurance contract rests upon:
o: Both the insurer and the insured
e: Although more often invoked against the insured, the insurer also must act in utmost good faith, for example by not misrepresenting policy terms.

t: An insurer's retention under a surplus treaty is Rs 1 crore and the treaty has 10 lines. For a risk of Rs 5 crore, the amount ceded to the treaty is:
e: Surplus reinsurance takes the amount above the retention: Rs 5 crore less Rs 1 crore = Rs 4 crore, well within the treaty capacity of 10 lines (Rs 10 crore).

t: The Insurance Institute of India was earlier known as the:
e: Established in 1955 as the Federation of Insurance Institutes, it was renamed the Insurance Institute of India in 1987.

t: An 'ex gratia' payment made by an insurer is:
o: A payment ordered by a court
A statutory penalty paid to IRDAI
A payment made as a matter of grace where the insurer has no legal liability under the policy
The payment of interest on delayed claims
e: Ex gratia payments are voluntary settlements made for commercial or compassionate reasons without admitting liability.

t: A manufacturer's stocks lie at three godowns in different towns and move between them; the quantities at each vary daily. The suitable fire cover is a:
o: Specific policy for each godown with fixed sums
e: A floater policy provides one sum insured that floats over stocks at several specified locations.

t: Which of the following is a peril and not a hazard?
e: A peril is the actual cause of loss; hazards (physical, moral, morale) are conditions that increase the chance or severity of loss from a peril.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 norms, a surveyor must be appointed within what time of a claim intimation?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Appointment within 24 hours; survey report within 15 days; insurer's decision within 7 days of the report.

t: The four nationalised general insurance subsidiaries of GIC commenced business with effect from:
e: GIBNA was passed in 1972 and the nationalised general insurance industry started functioning through GIC and its four subsidiaries from 1 January 1973.

t: The part of a policy document that contains the insurer's promise to indemnify the insured against the insured perils is the:
e: The operative clause sets out the insurer's undertaking; the recital refers to the proposal and premium, and the attestation carries the signature.

t: The declaration signed by the proposer at the foot of the proposal form states that:
o: The agent has filled in the form on his own responsibility
The answers are true and shall form the basis of the contract
The insurer accepts the risk from the date of signature
The premium will never be increased
e: The declaration makes the proposer's answers the basis of the contract, converting them into warranties of truth.
